title: Bat Boy at New York City Center #batboymusical #batboy #nycc #theatre...
transcript: The musical Bat Boy is so utterly ridiculous that it really has no business being this good. I was at the invited dress rehearsal last night at City Center, and the fact that this was the first full run-through in front of an audience is crazy because to me, it's Broadway ready. This musical, first produced in 1997, is literally about a boy who's also part bat. Despite being taken in by a family, he continues to confuse and disgust the local community, and all kinds of crazy stuff goes down. And you'll think Act 1 is crazy, but just wait until Act 2. As someone who knew nothing about the show beforehand, I was in for quite a ride. It’s absurd and so funny, and I love how the score is infused with humor, not just the script. This production, under the direction of Alex Timbers, has a feast of comedic performances — I thought Taylor Trensch, Gabi Carrubba, and Christopher Sieber were standouts, but there are quite a few notable folks in here doing just what they do best. On the way home, I was trying to reflect on what the themes of this piece are, and there might be something here about not judging a book by its cover or the dangers of herd mentality, but arguably, this just exists for our sheer entertainment. And that's great — there's something undeniably joy-inducing that comes out of a remarkably silly piece being executed at such a high level of commitment, and that's exactly what this production is. Bat Boy is running at New York City Center through November 9th. With that, another program for my collection.
